title: The people of the English line
dek: Twenty ancestors on Derrick's Wear and Hawkins sides, each graded on the same five-word ladder, each with what is not known.
note: Everyone here was born before 1900 and is long dead. Where a record was read the page says which; where a statement is a family tree's word, a best candidate or not proved, it says that instead, and the grade on the person is the grade of the weakest link a reader would otherwise take for granted.

people.name: Henry Robert Wear
people.why: A record was read for every step of his life from birth to burial.
people.dek: Born in Bermondsey, a fatherless boy at Watford, a printer's assistant at Letchworth, a soldier in 1914, and a machine minder who sailed for the Cape in April 1939.
facts: Birth registered at vol 1D p230. Mother's maiden name Hawkins: son of Robert Wear and Emma Hawkins.
Robert Wear, aged 31 (St Olave Southwark, vol 1D p141), about six months after his son's birth. The boy never knew him.
Aged one, with his widowed mother inside his uncle John Hawkins's household at 44 Ebury Road (RG12 piece 1120, folio 37).
Step-son of John Hull, a railway labourer, at 22 Mount Pleasant, aged 11 (RG13 piece 1312).
A boarder at 9 Ridge Road, aged 21 (RG14/7576/0009).

At the Congregational Church, Baldock. Two papers reported it and one prints him as 'Harry Ware'. He was in uniform, on furlough from Bury St Edmunds, and his battalion landed in France on 6 November.
The eldest, Leonard, has his own page. The others are not named here.
The Durban Castle, London to the Cape, occupation machine minder (transcribed 'machine minister'). Martha Maud followed on the Dunvegan Castle on 10 August with four of the children.
Aged 80. Buried at West Park Cemetery on 13 September in grave 56045, which his son Leonard bought that day (Private Graves Register, folio W 8).
gaps: His Master of the High Court estate file, MHG 10245/69, has been asked for and has not been seen.
The line from his son Leonard to Derrick rests on DNA and inference, not on a document. See the DNA page.

people.name: Martha Maud Castle
people.why: Her baptism, marriage, passage and burial are all records; only the exact birth day is a tree's word.
people.dek: The sixth of nine children, born at Baldock; she raised six children at Letchworth and sailed for Durban thirteen days before her brother died in London.
facts: Baptised there on 22 September 1895. The day of birth comes from a second-cousin match's family tree; the baptism fixes the year.
At the Congregational Church, Baldock. The Hertfordshire Express gives her address as Norton Street, Baldock, the first address this archive has for her.
At 72 Pix Road, in the same street as her husband's mother.
The Dunvegan Castle, London to Durban, with four of her children. Britain declared war on 3 September.

George William Castle, of 85 Jackmans-place, Letchworth, in St Bartholomew's Hospital, thirteen days after her ship sailed. He died without a will; administration went to Margaret Castle, widow, and Cyril George Castle, printer.
Aged 90. Buried in her husband's grave, 56045, at West Park.
gaps: The exact day of her birth rests on one tree; no record read here gives it.
Cyril George Castle, who shared her brother's administration, is not claimed as the brother's son.
see: The Leonard page, with the sailing and the probate

people.name: Robert Wear
people.why: His birth, marriage and death are all registered, and he is in his father's household in 1871.
people.dek: A harness-maker's youngest son from Jamaica Road, who married Emma Hawkins of Aldenham in 1881 and died eight years later, six months after his son was born.
facts: Birth registered in vol 1D. Mother's maiden name Bloom, which is the only place that name appears.
Aged 12, a scholar, in the house of his father William Wear, a harness maker, where his three older brothers worked at the same bench (RG10 piece 641, folio 40).
At St Olave, Southwark, vol 1D p455.
Louisa in 1883 at Wimbledon, Rosetta in 1886 at Bermondsey, and Henry Robert in Q3 1889 at Bermondsey.
gaps: His own occupation is not recorded in anything this archive holds; his father and his three older brothers were harness makers.
Why his first child was born at Wimbledon and the others at Bermondsey is not known.
The cause of his death is not known.

people.name: Emma Hawkins
people.why: Her baptism, both marriages' children, three censuses, the 1939 Register and her death are all records.
people.dek: Born at Aldenham, widowed at thirty-one, a stepfather's wife at St Albans, and blind in Pix Road, Letchworth, in 1939. Eighty-five years, two husbands buried, five children.
facts: Baptised there in 1859, daughter of John and Emma Hawkins. The day comes from the 1939 Register, given by Emma herself at eighty.
Aged 12, a scholar, one of six of the family's children still at home (RG10 piece 1380, folio 10).
At St Olave, Southwark. Three children follow, in 1883, 1886 and 1889.
Home to her brother's house at Watford
With her three children at 44 Ebury Road, in the household of her brother John Hawkins, a carter.
A railway labourer. Albert is born in 1895 and Edith in 1897, both at St Albans. In 1901 she is 'Emma Hull' at 22 Mount Pleasant, St Albans (RG13 piece 1312).

At 63 Pix Road, aged 80, widowed and incapacitated, living with her daughter Louisa and her son-in-law William Shenton. Her son Henry Robert raised his own children at 72 Pix Road, in the same street.
This archive wrote her mother's dates and history over her entry, because mother and daughter share a forename, and published the result for part of a day. Corrected.
gaps: Her marriage to John Hull has not been read; it is inferred from the births of 1895 and 1897 and the 1901 census.
When John Hull died is not established.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: George William Castle
people.why: His marriage and his death are index entries matched by name, age and district, with no certificate read. His birthplace and his parents are one researcher's tree, and the census disagrees with it.
people.dek: A farm labourer's son raised by his grandparents at Norton End after his mother died when he was under a year old.
facts: Birth registered at Hitchin. A baptism at St Mary's, Baldock, on 4 January 1863 (‘parents George & Martha, abode Willian’) comes from another researcher's tree, not from a register read here.
Martha Castle, registered at Hitchin. His father took him to her parents rather than his own.
With his grandparents at Norton End
Aged 8, 'grandson' in the house of James and Elizabeth Giddins, with his widowed father listed as their son-in-law (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

At Hitchin, registered in the December quarter of 1882, vol 3a p567, where the free index carries both names on one page. A tree gives October, which sits inside the quarter. The certificate has not been read.
At Middle Row in 1891 and at Norton in 1901, from the same tree.
His wife told the census nine children born, eight living and one dead. The dead one is Sidney Charles, who died at two.

Aged 54, registered at Hitchin, vol 3a p607: a George W Castle, which fits a man born in Q4 1862. A search of England and Wales for a George Castle aged 54 between March 1916 and December 1917 returns this entry alone, and Hitchin has no George Castle death in 1916 at all. A match holder's own tree gave 1917 independently. The identification is by name, age and district; the certificate has not been read.
gaps: The marriage certificate has not been read. It would name both fathers, and with them Caroline's.

His death certificate has not been read, so the place and cause are not known, and the year 1917 rests on an index entry matched by name, age and district. One tree still says 1916; the index has no George Castle death at Hitchin in 1916.
The census disagrees with the tree twice: it gives his birthplace as Baldock, not Willian, and his birth year as 1863, not 1862.
see: His daughter Martha Maud, and the probate of his son

people.name: Caroline Wallis
people.died: 1957, registered at Hitchin as Caroline James
people.why: Her later life is documented and her marriage is an index entry. Her parents are not established and her year of birth is disputed.
people.dek: She remarried in 1920 and died in 1957 as Caroline James, which is why every tree that carries her as Caroline Wallis was hunting a death registered under another surname.
facts: The day and month come from the 1939 Register, which gives 28 February 1863. The 1957 death index gives 1862. Her age of 48 at the 1911 census fits 1863 and not 1862; her 56 years 4 months in 1921 fits neither, since it works out at February 1865. Two Hitchin births are registered under Wallis: a Caroline in the March quarter of 1862 (vol 3a p230) and an unnamed female in the March quarter of 1863 (vol 3a p247). Neither has been tied to her.
At Hitchin, registered in the December quarter of 1882, vol 3a p567, with both names on the one page of the free index. A tree gives October. The certificate has not been read.
Her answer to the census question; one child, Sidney Charles, had died at two.
James James, at Hitchin (vol 3A p2077), three years after George William's death in 1917.

At 9 Boscombe Place, wife of James James, born at Weston, aged 56 years 4 months. Two children in the house are enumerated as his step-children and carry the surname Castle (RG15 piece 7079, schedule 125).
gaps: Her parents are not established, and no baptism has been found. FreeCEN has no Caroline Wallis born in Hertfordshire in the 1860s, but its Hertfordshire coverage is patchy and that is not a finding. It does hold a John Wallis, born at Weston about 1863, lodging at Clothall in 1891: a Wallis was born at Weston in her year, and he is not claimed as kin.
Her first marriage certificate has not been read. It would name her father, and ordering it is a purchase for the family to decide.

people.name: William Wear
people.why: He is in two censuses and his son's birth registration; his parents and his marriage are not on the same footing.
people.dek: A sadler in 1851 and a harness maker by 1871, who brought three of his sons up to his own bench in Jamaica Road.
facts: Walworth in 1851, Newington in 1871. Walworth is a district inside Newington parish and is the more precise.

Son of John Wear and Elizabeth, with three siblings baptised the same day. Held as probable: it is a transcribed index and not the register, it gives no occupation, and Newington had a second Wear household.
A marriage that is not proved
A Sarah Bloom married one of four men registered on Stepney vol 2 p430, and one of the four is 'William Weare'. The index does not say which. A certificate would name both fathers.
At Bermondsey (HO107 piece 1560, folio 212), with his wife Sarah and two small sons.
A harness maker in Jamaica Road
Aged 48 (RG10 piece 641, folio 40), with four sons, three of them harness makers at his bench, and a niece of his wife's from Yarmouth.
gaps: His parents are a best candidate, held as probable.
His marriage is not proved.
His death is not established.

people.name: Sarah Bloom
people.why: Her maiden name is from one birth registration and one niece, and her birthplace is disputed between two censuses.
people.dek: Her birthplace is given as Deptford in Kent in 1851 and Bermondsey in Surrey in 1871, which is not a spelling variant.
facts: Born at Deptford, or at Bermondsey
1851 says Deptford, Kent; 1871 says Bermondsey, Surrey. They are different counties.
A marriage that is not proved
A Sarah Bloom married one of four men registered on Stepney vol 2 p430; one of them is 'William Weare'.
Aged 29, wife of William Wear, with two small sons (HO107 piece 1560, folio 212).
Her maiden name is on her son's birth
Robert Wear's birth registration gives the mother's maiden name as Bloom. A married woman's maiden name is never in a census.
A niece from Yarmouth in the house
Sarah Ann Bloom, aged 17, born at Yarmouth, Norfolk (RG10 piece 641). With a Norfolk niece and Norfolk marriages in the index, the Blooms may not be a London family at all.
gaps: Her parents are not known.
Where she was born is not settled.
Her death is not established.

people.name: John Hawkins
people.why: He is in three censuses and a banns entry; his parentage is a best candidate.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer of Aldenham, baptised in 1819, who called the banns for Emma Larkin in 1842 and raised at least eleven children in a hamlet and then at the Red Lion Cottages.
facts: Son of William Hawkins and Mary. He is the only John the register offers in the window, the other Johns being excluded by age. Held as a best candidate: the register cannot show that this child is the Red Lion man.

Most likely the John aged 20 at Aldenham Checkers, in a household of three with Katherine Nicholls and William Kimpton (HO107 piece 438). The 1841 census, which the work list nominated, could not give his parents.
Both resident at Aldenham. What is read is the banns entry; the wedding itself has not been seen.
Head, agricultural labourer, aged 39 (HO107 piece 1714, folio 19), with Emma and four children. The age sits eight years from his 1871 age, and the baptism agrees with 1871.
Aged 51, agricultural labourer, eight in the household, every one of them born in the parish (RG10 piece 1380, folio 10, schedule 58).
gaps: His death is not established.
His parents are a best candidate and not proved.
His age is given as 39 in 1851 and 51 in 1871, which cannot both be right.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Emma Larkin
people.why: Her baptism, her banns and two censuses are records; her parents' marriage is a best candidate.
people.dek: Carried on this site for weeks as 'Emma Hawkins', which was her married name; she was born Emma Larkin, the sixth of eleven children.
facts: Daughter of Robert and Mary Larkin; the only Emma Larkin of her generation in the parish, and the birth year matches the 1871 census to the year.
Both resident at Aldenham; the banns were called, and the wedding has not been seen.
There was no Emma among the twenty Hawkinses of Aldenham in 1841, which was the clue that she was a Hawkins only by marriage.
gaps: Her parents are a best candidate: the register names a Robert and a Mary, and the 1814 banns name a Robert Larkin and a Mary Burch, but no document joins them.
Her death is not established.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: George Castle
people.died: Q4 1885, Hitchin, aged 46 (an index entry matched by name, age and district)
people.why: The 1871 census names him as son-in-law and father; his death is an index entry matched by name, age and district.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer who was widowed within a year and took his baby son to his dead wife's parents.
facts: The 1871 census gives age 30 and Baldock.
Registered at Hitchin. The index puts a Castle and a Giddins on the same page; the 1871 census relationship is what ties them.
George William, registered at Hitchin, within three months of the wedding.
Martha dies, nine to twelve months after the birth. It was not childbirth.
Aged 30, an agricultural labourer, in the house of James and Elizabeth Giddins, with his son George aged 8 (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

Aged 46, registered at Hitchin, vol 3a p249: the only George Castle death at Hitchin between 1884 and 1886, and the age fits a man born about 1839 to 1840. A tree had said 'died when his son was 23', which agrees. Matched by name, age and district; the certificate has not been read.
gaps: His own parents are not known.
His death certificate has not been read, so the entry above is matched and not proved.

people.name: Martha Giddings
people.why: The 1871 census names her only through the relationships of the people left behind, and that is enough.
people.dek: She is in neither household she belonged to. Her existence is attested by what the 1871 census says about her widower and her son.
facts: Aged about 20 and not in their household at 9 Cottages, Norton End (RG9 piece 816, folio 69), which lists George, John and Emma.
Registered at Hitchin. The index gives a Castle and a Giddins on the same page.
George William, registered at Hitchin. Baptised in January 1863, from a tree.
A Martha Castle death registered at Hitchin, vol 3A p188. A second Martha Castle death in 1865 cannot be ruled out on the index alone, because the death index before 1866 carries no age.
Attested by the people left behind
George Castle, 30, is enumerated as son-in-law in her parents' house and a boy of 8 as grandson. Both relationships run only through her.
gaps: Her death date is the Q3 1863 entry, which cannot be separated from the 1865 one on the index alone.
The register indexes spell her Giddings and the census spells the family Giddins; both are carried here.

people.name: James Giddins
people.why: He is in the 1861 and 1871 censuses at the same address.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer at Norton End who raised a grandson who was not his to raise.
facts: Aged 46, an agricultural labourer born at Baldock, with Elizabeth and the children George 14, John 12 and Emma 6 (RG9 piece 816, folio 69).
At Norton End, a decade on
Aged 57, with his wife, his widowed son-in-law George Castle and a grandson of 8 (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

This archive wrote that his daughter Emma was born on 7 February 1859. That is Emma Hawkins of Aldenham, a different woman in a different parish; the Emma in this house is Emma Giddins, born about 1855.
gaps: His parents and his marriage have not been looked for in a register. A James Giddings aged 68 was registered at Hitchin in Q1 1883 (vol 3a p257), which fits a man born about 1815, and an Elizabeth Giddings aged 68 in Q2 1883 (vol 3a p250) fits his wife. They are the only James and Elizabeth of that age under any spelling at Hitchin from Q2 1871 to 1895. No record ties them to Norton End, so his death is a candidate and not established.

people.name: Elizabeth Giddins
people.why: She is in the 1861 and 1871 censuses with her husband.
people.dek: Born at Norton, and in 1871 doing platting, the straw-plaiting that kept Hertfordshire women in work for a century.
facts: Aged 46, wife of James Giddins, born at Norton (RG9 piece 816, folio 69).
Aged 57, her occupation straw-plaiting, with a widowed son-in-law and a grandson in the house (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).
gaps: Her maiden name is not known: she appears under her husband's surname in every record.
Her parents and her marriage are not established. An Elizabeth Giddings aged 68, registered at Hitchin in Q2 1883 (vol 3a p250), fits her death and is not tied to her by any record.

people.name: John Wear
people.why: An index of the Newington baptism register names him as father of four children baptised together, one of whom is William; no record joins him to William beyond that.
people.dek: A Newington man, the best candidate for William Wear's father, who is on this site only as the name on a baptism index.
facts: At Newington, Surrey: Matilda (born 1820), William (1823), Thomas (1825) and Mary Ann (1827). Matilda and Thomas, opened in full, both name John Wear as father and Elizabeth as mother.
Elizabeth (born 1812) and John (born 1817) were baptised together in 1819, in the same parish, with a father named John.
gaps: It is an INDEX of the register and not the register, so it gives no occupation, and the trade is the lever this archive nominated.
Newington had a second Wear household under a John Southey Wear, so a forename match there is not an identification.
His marriage, his trade and his death are not known.

people.name: Elizabeth Wear
people.why: Her name is on two of four transcripts of the baptisms of 10 April 1833, and on no other record.
people.dek: Known only as the mother named on two baptism transcripts at Newington, and held as probable.
facts: Two of the four baptism transcripts, those of Matilda and Thomas, were opened in full and both give the mother as Elizabeth. Mary Ann's was not opened.
gaps: Her maiden name, her birth, her marriage and her death are all unknown.
Which of the Newington children were hers is the same question as whether the household is the right one.

people.name: William Hawkins
people.why: The register offers exactly one William-and-Mary pair among 44 Hawkins marriage entries, married in the right year; that is a best candidate and not proof.
people.dek: Called the banns for Mary Appleyard at Aldenham in April 1800; nine children were baptised to a William and Mary Hawkins between 1801 and 1819.
facts: At Aldenham, both resident in the parish. It is the only William-and-Mary pair among the 44 Hawkins marriage entries. The set indexes each calling separately, so this one wedding appears twice.
George 1801, Sarah 1803, Mary 1805, Jane 1808, Thomas 1810, Mary 1812, William 1814, Charlotte 1817 and John 1819, to a William and Mary Hawkins. The reused name Mary suggests the first Mary died.
gaps: Banns are the announcement and not the wedding; the marriage entry itself has not been seen.
His own baptism and parents are unknown.
That the John of 1819 is the Red Lion man is a best candidate.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Mary Appleyard
people.why: Her maiden name rests on one banns entry; her own baptism has not been found.
people.dek: A surname this archive had never held. She married into Aldenham from somewhere her own baptism has not been found.
facts: At Aldenham, both resident. 'Of this parish' in a banns entry is residence at the time and not birth.
No Appleyard baptism of her generation at Aldenham

All 18 Appleyard baptisms there were read: a John-and-Hannah family ending in 1749 and a William-and-Ann family beginning in 1809, with nothing in between. The register is well covered for those decades, so the absence is real.
gaps: Her own baptism has not been found. A surname-only free-index search (16 October 2026) found one Appleyard baptism of any forename in Hertfordshire, Middlesex and Buckinghamshire between 1750 and 1800, an Ann at Marylebone, and nine Mary Appleyards in all England 1762 to 1782, every one in Yorkshire. That shows where the index finds the name and not where she was born. The Aldenham registers hold 18 Appleyard baptisms and that index does not carry them.
Her parents, her birthplace and her death are unknown.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Robert Larkin
people.why: The register offers two candidate baptisms and nothing separates them.
people.dek: Called the banns for Mary Burch at Aldenham in January 1814; eleven children were baptised to a Robert and a Mary Larkin between 1814 and 1833.
facts: At Aldenham, both resident. It is the only Robert-and-Mary pair among 30 Larkin marriage entries.
Sarah, Mary, Elizabeth, Joseph, Robert William, Emma, Amy, James, John, a second Joseph and Thomas. Two Josephs, so the first had most likely died.
A Robert baptised in 1789 to Robert and Ann would be 24 at the marriage; a Robert baptised in 1781 to James and Sarah would be 33. Both are ordinary marriage ages and this archive picks neither.
gaps: Which baptism is his is not known. The 1841 census cannot separate them, because the only Robert Larkin at Aldenham in 1841 is his son, aged 20.
The one Robert Larkin burial at Aldenham, on 1 September 1793, carries no age, so it cannot be told whether it is anyone here.
His death is not established.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Mary Burch
people.why: Her maiden name rests on one banns entry; her own baptism has not been found.
people.dek: Another surname this archive had never held. She married into Aldenham in 1814 from somewhere her baptism has not been found.
facts: No Burch baptism of her generation at Aldenham
All 7 Burch baptisms there are of 1811 or later, so none can be hers.
gaps: Her own baptism has not been found. A free-index search of Hertfordshire, Middlesex and Buckinghamshire (16 October 2026) found no Mary BURCH baptised 1770 to 1800 and five Marys baptised BIRCH who could be her: Abbots Langley 1782 and 1784, Watford 1783, Great Stanmore 1791 and Bovingdon 1791. None is chosen. The same search on Findmypast, surname-only and county-wide, has still not been done.
Her parents, her birthplace and her death are unknown.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers
